acceptance_criteria.criterion: Running the compiled CLI entry point (node dist/index.js) with a valid config.json starts the HTTP server and logs a success message including the port number.
The staticDir is correctly resolved to gui/public/ relative to the project root using path.resolve(__dirname, '..', 'gui', 'public').
Opening http://localhost:<serverPort> in a browser serves index.html and the full GUI loads.
If the server fails to start (e.g., port in use), an error message is written to stderr and the process exits with code 1.
The existing --verbose flag continues to print configuration details before server startup.

summary: Modified src/index.ts to wire the HTTP server startup into the CLI entry point. Added imports for node:path and startServer from ./server/index.js. After config loading and verbose logging, staticDir is resolved using CJS-native __dirname (project has no "type":"module" in package.json — module:Node16 + no type=module → CJS output, so __dirname is natively available). startServer is called with appConfig, staticDir, serverPort, and pollIntervalSeconds. On success, logs the server URL including the port. On failure, writes to stderr and exits with code 1. The existing --verbose flag and synchronous config error handling are preserved unchanged. All 517 tests pass.

comments.note: src/index.ts: The project uses module:Node16 but has no "type":"module" in package.json, making all .ts files compile to CommonJS. The WP spec mentioned using fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) for ESM __dirname compatibility, but that would fail compilation in CJS mode. CJS __dirname is used instead, which is correct given the actual module system in use. Consider adding a comment near the __dirname usage to explain why import.meta.url is not used here, to prevent future confusion.

summary: Reviewed 8 files across src/index.ts, src/server/index.ts, src/server/staticServer.ts, src/server/router.ts, src/server/requestUtils.ts, src/server/routes/* (branches, status, repositories), src/config/config.ts. 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium (noted), 3 Low (noted). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: OWASP REVIEW SUMMARY — All 10 categories reviewed. No Critical or High issues identified. Blocking issue count: 0.

A01 — Broken Access Control / A05 — Security Misconfiguration (MEDIUM): src/server/index.ts — The HTTP server binds to all interfaces (0.0.0.0) by default via Node.js http.Server. For a local developer tool this is commonly intentional, but any other machine on the same network can reach the API endpoints, which expose potentially sensitive filesystem paths, repository names, workspace IDs, and branch-switch operations. The API has no authentication layer. Recommendation: Restrict the bind address to 127.0.0.1 (loopback) by passing it as the second argument to server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', ...) unless LAN access is an explicit product requirement. If LAN access is intended, document it clearly and consider adding a simple token or shared-secret check to the API routes.

A05 — Security Misconfiguration (MEDIUM): src/server/index.ts & src/server/staticServer.ts — No security-relevant HTTP response headers are set (e.g. X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy). For a tool serving a local GUI this is a low-exploitation risk, but a CSP header on the static server would prevent a class of injection attacks if the GUI ever renders user-supplied content. Recommendation: Add at minimum X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and X-Frame-Options: DENY to both static and API responses. A restrictive default-src CSP on HTML responses is also advisable.

A01 — Broken Access Control (LOW / INFO): src/server/staticServer.ts lines 66–75 — The path-traversal guard is well-implemented: decodeURIComponent is called before path.resolve, and the resolved path is checked against baseDir + path.sep. Double-encoded sequences (%252e%252e) would decode to literal '%2e%2e' (not '../') because decodeURIComponent only decodes one layer; path.resolve would then treat the literal percent signs as normal filename characters and the file would not exist, so it would return false harmlessly. No traversal bypass found.

A03 — Injection (LOW / INFO): src/server/requestUtils.ts lines 41–46 — Raw request body is truncated to 120 characters and included in the error message returned to the client ('Invalid JSON body: <raw>'). This is a minor information-leakage risk — a large non-JSON payload's first 120 bytes are echoed back. In a local-only tool the risk is negligible, but replacing the echo with a static 'Request body is not valid JSON.' message would be cleaner. No injection risk in the direction of server execution.

A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring Failures (LOW): src/server/index.ts — No audit logging is present for mutating API calls (repository add/remove/update, workspace creation, branch-switch). For a local developer tool this is acceptable, but if the tool is ever exposed over a network, a structured audit log of destructive operations would be valuable for incident investigation.

A04 — Insecure Design (INFO): src/index.ts line 31 — staticDir is resolved using path.resolve(__dirname, '..', 'gui', 'public'). This path is fixed at startup and cannot be influenced by user input, so there is no user-controlled path injection risk. The usage is correct and safe.

A02 — Cryptographic Failures (INFO): No secrets, tokens, or credentials are stored or transmitted. config.json holds filesystem paths and port numbers only. HTTP (not HTTPS) is used, which is appropriate for a localhost dev tool; no sensitive session tokens are transmitted. No cryptographic weaknesses found.

A06 — Vulnerable & Outdated Components (INFO): WP-012 introduces no new third-party dependencies — all changes are in TypeScript source files using only Node.js built-in modules (node:http, node:fs, node:path). No CVE exposure from this work package.

A07 — Identification & Authentication Failures (INFO): No authentication or session management mechanism exists. Given the tool's stated use case as a local developer utility, this is by design. The absence of auth is noted as a systemic property, not a defect introduced by this WP.

A08 — Software & Data Integrity Failures (INFO): No deserialization of untrusted data beyond JSON request bodies, which are capped at 1 MB and validated with isPlainObject checks before use. No unsafe eval or dynamic require. No pipeline artifact concerns introduced by this WP.

A10 — Server-Side Request Forgery (INFO): No outbound HTTP requests are made from the server based on user-supplied URLs in this WP. Repository URL values accepted via POST /api/repositories are stored as data and passed to git tooling — SSRF via git URL is a separate pre-existing concern outside the scope of this WP's changes.

summary: Code review PASS. Implementation is correct, minimal, and well-structured. No change required — already handled correctly in existing tests.
